title: Launch Brief (Draft Slides) — Canonical Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output Examples
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Canonical Examples Refresh: Streaming + Tool Calling + Structured Output
Internal launch brief (DevEx + Docs + Product)

Speaker notes:
- This is the cross-SDK + docs refresh to make our examples consistent, runnable, and resilient.
- Focus: reduce support tickets caused by snippet drift and ambiguous event handling.


Slide 2 — TL;DR (What shipped)
- New canonical example patterns for:
  - Token streaming (delta handling + final response capture)
  - Tool calling (single tool + parallel tools; safe argument accumulation)
  - Structured output (schema-based validation + retry strategy)
- Parity across Python / TypeScript / Go (same concepts + same terminology)
- Docs-site rewrite to reference canonical examples and remove legacy snippets
- Snippet test runner (CI) to prevent future drift
- Troubleshooting updates for top issues (disconnects, partial args, schema mismatch)

Speaker notes:
- “Canonical examples” live in redwood-examples; SDK READMEs + docs link to them.
- CI is the enforcement mechanism so we don’t regress back into drift.


Slide 3 — Why we did this (Customer + Support signal)
- Support volume increased due to:
  - Stream disconnects behind proxies / buffering infrastructure
  - Confusion on streaming event shapes (delta vs final, tool_call deltas)
  - Partial tool-call arguments causing JSON parse failures
  - Structured output “schema mismatch” after copying older docs snippets
- Resulting pain:
  - Customers writing fragile loops (“works until it doesn’t”)
  - Inconsistent fixes suggested across SDKs
  - Longer time-to-first-success for PLG users

Speaker notes:
- Cite: SUP-18421 (disconnect + incomplete args), SUP-18433 (schema mismatch), SUP-18455 (TS partial JSON deltas).
- Goal is fewer escalations and fewer “which doc is correct?” moments.


Slide 4 — What changed: streaming (new canonical pattern)
- Canonical streaming loop now:
  - Handles token deltas as deltas (don’t assume full text in each event)
  - Captures final response object (usage, finish_reason, tool calls, etc.)
  - Includes timeout + cancellation guidance (AbortSignal/context)
- Docs now explicitly define event semantics:
  - What you can rely on during the stream
  - What you should only rely on at finalization

Speaker notes:
- We saw repeated bugs where “final message missing” because users only concatenate deltas and don’t handle end-of-stream final payload.
- The examples demonstrate both “print streaming text” and “keep the final object for logging/metrics”.


Slide 5 — What changed: tool calling (delta semantics + safety)
- Tool calling examples now demonstrate:
  - Tool-call argument deltas can be partial and not valid JSON until complete
  - Accumulate arguments per tool_call_id, parse only when complete
  - Parallel tool calling pattern with concurrency control
- Safety-first guidance baked into examples:
  - Tool allowlist (explicit mapping name -> handler)
  - Validate tool args before execution
  - Redact sensitive data from logs

Speaker notes:
- Product terminology: we’re standardizing on “tool calling” in user-facing docs (with “function calling” noted as legacy/alias where applicable).
- Emphasize: never run arbitrary user-provided tool names; examples show safe dispatch.


Slide 6 — What changed: structured output (schema + validation + retries)
- Structured output examples now:
  - Provide JSON Schema (or SDK-idiomatic validator)
  - Validate the parsed output before using it
  - Retry strategy when parsing/validation fails
  - Guidance for strict vs lenient parsing (what we recommend by default)
- Docs add:
  - Clear “schema mismatch” explanation + remediation
  - Schema versioning note (avoid silently changing schemas in published docs)

Speaker notes:
- Key intent: prevent “silent parse failures” and “it parsed but the fields are wrong” issues.
- We show the minimum safe approach without turning docs into a full reliability guide.


Slide 7 — Docs-site: IA + page updates
- Streaming + Tools + Structured Output now grouped under one navigation section
- Legacy snippets removed or replaced; cross-links updated
- New troubleshooting callouts embedded where users fail most often

Speaker notes:
- This reduces the “which page should I read?” problem and makes it clear these topics are connected.


Slide 8 — Canonical source of truth (and how drift is prevented)
- Source of truth: redwood-examples repo
  - language folders (python/ts/go)
  - consistent naming + narrative
- Enforcement: snippet test runner
  - fast mock-server run (default)
  - optional staging run (gated)
  - CI fails if examples break or drift

Speaker notes:
- This is the primary long-term fix. The doc refresh is necessary, but CI is what keeps it correct.


Slide 9 — Compatibility + expectations (what users need to know)
- Backward compatibility:
  - Examples aim to be compatible with current stable SDK interfaces
  - Where behavior differs across SDKs, docs call it out explicitly
- Copy/paste runnable:
  - Examples include minimal deps + env var setup
  - No insecure patterns (no arbitrary tool execution; no secret logging)

Speaker notes:
- If we couldn’t keep an older pattern, we added a “version requirement” note in the relevant snippet/docs section.


Slide 10 — Launch plan (internal)
- Release components:
  - SDK patch releases (Python / TS / Go)
  - Docs-site deploy
  - redwood-examples updates + CI enabled
- Comms:
  - #devex announcement with links
  - docs changelog entry
  - Support enablement blurb (what to link customers to)

Speaker notes:
- Connor is coordinating final go/no-go and timing with releases.
- Support callout: the first-line response for related tickets should point to canonical examples + troubleshooting.


Slide 11 — Metrics: how we’ll know it worked
- Short-term (1–2 weeks):
  - Fewer “example doesn’t work” support threads
  - Reduction in repeat questions on partial tool args / schema mismatch
- Medium-term (1–2 months):
  - Decreased ticket volume for streaming disconnect handling
  - Fewer regressions due to snippet tests catching drift pre-merge
- Internal operational signals:
  - New gateway metrics for disconnect reasons and tool-call parse errors

Speaker notes:
- We should tag support tickets related to this for a couple of weeks to see deltas.


Slide 12 — How to report bugs / feedback (routing)
- Bugs in examples:
  - File issue / PR in redwood-examples (preferred)
  - Or drop in #devex with “examples-bug” and link to snippet
- Bugs in SDK behavior:
  - SDK repo issue + reproduction + SDK version
  - Tag SDK owner (Dana / Mateusz / Ibrahim)
- Docs feedback:
  - PR in redwood-docs or note in #docs
- Customer escalations:
  - Link ticket + logs in #support; include proxy/LB details for streaming disconnects

Speaker notes:
- Please include: language + SDK version + snippet link + what you expected vs what happened.


Slide 13 — Open items / follow-ups (post-launch)
- Confirm any remaining parity gaps called out in the SDK parity matrix
- Quickstarts/templates: ensure they reference canonical snippets and stay runnable
- Evaluate whether we need a dedicated “stream reconnect/resume” guide page (beyond callouts)

Speaker notes:
- We intentionally kept scope to docs/ergonomics; follow-ups can be separate workstreams if we see persistent pain.


Slide 14 — Thank you + owners
- Exec owner: Monica Patel
- Tech lead: Ibrahim Khan
- SDK owners: Dana Lo (TS), Mateusz Zielinski (Go), Python SDK team
- Docs program: Elliot Price, Wei Chen
- Security review: Marcus Lin
- Release coordination: Connor O’Brien

Speaker notes:
- Reminder: the biggest win is consistency across surfaces. If you see a drift risk, route it early.


Appendix slide (optional) — Reference links (internal)
- Canonical patterns spec (Confluence): streaming + tools + structured output
- Docs refresh plan + editorial checklist
- Support top issues doc: streaming disconnects + partial tool args
- ADR: canonical examples + snippet testing

Notes to self (Talia):
- Add final release dates + exact SDK versions once Connor confirms.
- Add 1 screenshot of the new docs IA section once docs PR merges.
- Ask Dev Patel for the support macro text (one-paragraph “what changed” + link bundle).
